transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This sounds like an earth fault where electricity is leaking to the metal casing, causing your RCD (fuse box switch) to trip for safety. Because this involves mains electricity and water, it is dangerous: please stop using the machine and do not keep resetting the fuse, as repeated tripping can cause further damage or fire risk. The most common cause in Indesit machines is a failing heater element that has developed an internal short to earth; this usually trips only when the heating stage starts. Less commonly, it could be the drain pump or the mains cable itself. Could you tell me: does the power go off immediately when you turn the dial on, or only after a few minutes once the water has started filling and heating?

It isn't immediately. It's always a few minutes into the wash, and only on the 40 or 60 degree programmes. I've been resetting the switch each time it happened, which is now quite a few times over the last month, so I'll stop doing that. I haven't noticed any burning smell or scorching.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Thank you for confirming those details. The fact that it only trips on hot washes (40 or 60 degrees) strongly points to the heating element developing an internal short circuit to earth when it gets hot; this is a very common failure in Indesit machines and explains why it doesn't happen on cold cycles. Because this involves mains electricity leaking into water, please do not use the machine again until it has been repaired. You need to leave it unplugged and have a qualified appliance engineer replace the heater element (or check the internal wiring if that is clear). This is not something you can safely fix yourself given the risk of electric shock.
